name: Paku
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Diedrich, Daniela. 2018. A grammar of Paku: a language of Central Kalimantan. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne. xiv+315 pp. Open access, Minerva Access handle 11343/225728.
catalog_locator: Ch. 2 Phonology, sec. 2.3 'Stress', p. 41; cross-checked ch. 1 pp. 17-18, sec. 2.5 'Syllables', ch. 4 p. 98, sec. 8.4.
catalog_quote: Primary stress within roots in Paku is on the penultimate syllable and is non-distinctive. Stress placement is very regular and predictable with only few exceptions in the data. What this means is that stress is not part of the lexical entry of a word. [...] Moreover there is both inter- and intra-speaker variation with regard to stress placement: not only do speakers sometimes vary from each other but also on occasion the same speaker will produce the same word differently without any obvious conditioning environment. An example of a root exhibiting a lot of variation is tekui ‘when’ which is sometimes produced as ['tekuj] and other times as [te'kuj]. A common example of irregular stress placement is bakoi ‘NEG’ in which the ultimate syllable is more prominent than the penultimate one. [...] Paku stress does not move to the right through suffixation. For instance, when -an is suffixed to the verbal root /'gawi/ ‘work’ to form /'gawian/ ‘work (n.)’, stress remains on the original penultimate syllable of /'gawi/. As a result, in /'gawian/ stress is now on the antepenultimate syllable. In the few instances of roots consisting of four syllables, in addition to primary stress on the penultimate syllable secondary stress is placed on the initial one, e.g. [kolo'waNun] ‘how’ and [wuwu'nijan] ‘bladder’.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the root; it is non-contrastive and not lexical. Suffixation (-an) does not shift stress rightward, so suffixed words surface with antepenultimate stress. Stress is described as not a salient feature, with some free inter- and intra-speaker variation.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In four-syllable roots, secondary stress on the initial syllable (e.g. [,kolo'waNun] 'how', [,wuwu'nijan] 'bladder').
new_statements.exceptions: Free variation in some roots (tekui 'when' ['tekuj]~[te'kuj]); bakoi 'NEG' regularly has final prominence; variability decreases with syllable count (none in four-syllable words); in content questions phrase stress falls on the question word (8.4).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the root, not the word: stress stays on the root penult under suffixation (-> word-antepenult in -an forms); most Paku affixation is prefixal so root-penult = word-penult in most forms. Author notes intonation unit seems more relevant in discourse; stress judged impressionistically (no instrumental study).
new_statements.identity_note: Diedrich 2018 describes Paku (paku1239, ISO pku) as spoken in four villages (Tampa area) in southeast Central Kalimantan, ~50 speakers, moribund; East Barito (reclassified out of Southeast Barito per Smith 2017). No dialect split relevant to the stress statement.

tone_statements.citation: Iper, Dunis. 2002. Struktur Bahasa Paku. Jakarta: Pusat Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan Nasional. ix+210 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 2.1 Deskripsi Fonem Fonem yang dideskripsikan dalam bagian ini adalah fonem segmental. Dalam bahasa Paku tidak terdapat fonem suprasegmental. Berdasarkan data yang ada, dalam bahasa Paku terdapat bunyi-bunyi (fon-fon) yang dicurigai merupakan fonem-fonem bahasa Paku.
tone_statements.translation: 2.1 Description of phonemes. The phonemes described in this part are segmental phonemes. In the Paku language there are no suprasegmental phonemes. Based on the available data, Paku has sounds (phones) suspected to be phonemes of Paku.
tone_statements.locator: p. 9, Bab II Fonologi, 2.1 Deskripsi Fonem
tone_statements.summary: States that Paku has no suprasegmental phonemes, i.e. no contrastive tone, stress or length; pitch figures only as sentence intonation (imperatives take high pitch or strong stress on the verb).

tone.quote: Fonem suprasegmen tidak dibuktikan secara fonemis, karena keterbatasan data yang diperoleh serta waktu yang tersedia. Dari hasil analisis ditemukan dua jenis fonem suprasegmen yang dominan, yaitu tekanan dan intonasi. … Intonasi pada kalimat berita adalah nada rendah-tinggi pada akhir kalimat. Pada kalimat tanya intonasi tersebut menjadi tinggi-rendah pada kata tanya dan rendah-tinggi pada akhir kalimat. Pada kalimat perintah intonasi yang ditemukan adalah nada tinggi-rendah pada akhir kalimat.
tone.locator: p. 121, Bab IV 4.1 Kesimpulan (scope statement p. 108 §3.2; pitch-level notation p. 111 §3.2.2)
tone.translation: The suprasegmental phonemes were not proven phonemically, because of the limited data obtained and the time available. From the analysis two dominant kinds of suprasegmental phoneme were found, namely stress and intonation. … Intonation in declarative sentences is low-high pitch at the end of the sentence. In questions it becomes high-low on the question word and low-high at the end of the sentence. In commands the intonation found is high-low pitch at the end of the sentence.
tone.summary: Treats only stress and intonation; high/mid/low pitch levels serve solely to notate intonation (30 sentences); lexical tone neither described nor denied; suprasegmentals 'not proven phonemic'.
tone.says: Treats only stress and intonation; high/mid/low pitch levels serve solely to notate intonation (30 sentences); lexical tone neither described nor denied; suprasegmentals 'not proven phonemic'.
